context: A refresh-token rotation race across concurrent callers. A good run models the protocol (TLA+/PlusCal or an equivalent bounded checker), maps model to code, reinserts the pre-fix behavior as a negative control the checker must reject on a named invariant, wires one pinned, path-filtered CI task for both, writes a short repo-local skill, and reports honestly what it ran.

checklist.name: Invariant stated
checklist.description: The model states a safety invariant in one sentence equivalent to: concurrent 401s never send a revoked refresh token, so a valid session is never signed out by a refresh race.

checklist.name: Bounded model of the protocol
checklist.description: A model file is added (for example a TLA+ or PlusCal spec with a TLC config, or a Lincheck test) that represents at least two concurrent callers, the stored tokens, server-side rotation and revocation, and the mutex; bounds are stated with a reason they suffice.

checklist.name: Mapping to code
checklist.description: The model carries a table or header mapping its variables and actions to TokenRefresher.refresh, TokenStore, and AuthApi.refresh, and TokenRefresher.kt gets a short comment naming the model.

checklist.name: Negative control
checklist.description: A variant reinserts the pre-fix behavior (no mutex, or no replaced-token check) and is expected to fail with a counterexample on the named invariant; the check treats a parse error or timeout as a failure, not as the expected red.

checklist.name: CI wiring
checklist.description: One repo task (for example a Gradle task) runs the clean model and the variant, CI calls it, the checker version is pinned, and the job is path-filtered on the model directory and the mapped auth code.

checklist.name: Repo-local skill
checklist.description: A short repo-local SKILL.md under a harness skills directory says how to run the models, what to do when mapped code changes, how to read a counterexample, and how to add a model.

checklist.name: Honest about execution
checklist.description: The final message says whether the checker actually ran here; if it did not, it gives the command and claims no state counts, pass, or counterexample output.
